title: How Wheaton Brick Houses Load Urban Dust Into Air Ducts
headline: Veirs Mill grit, Georgia Avenue pollen, and why older plaster joints leak
description: Wheaton, MD mixes 1940s–60s brick with Metro-corridor dust. Learn why older ducts collect urban grit and pollen, and when to clean them from Bethesda.

sections.heading: Wheaton is close-in Montgomery. The dust is urban.
paragraphs: Around Westfield, the Metro, Veirs Mill Road, and Georgia Avenue the housing is mixed on purpose: 1940s–60s brick colonials and ramblers, later split-levels, garden apartments, and newer infill. Older ductwork was cut through plaster and joists. Joints leak. Bus-corridor grit and downtown construction add a second load the returns never sort from tree pollen.

Aspen Hill, Kemp Mill, and Glenmont fill the same close-in ring. Basements stay cool. Maryland summers stay wet. Cold trunks sweat, and the first AC week after a pollen burst is when registers look dirty again.

sections.heading: Plaster-era trunks were never a sealed system
paragraphs: A 1950s Wheaton brick house often gained central air later. The metal snakes through bays that were never designed for it. Dust collects at every kink. Garden-apartment dryers pack lint in shared chases. Portable gear matters on streets where a truck cannot stage next to the stoop.
If wiping the registers only lasts a few days, start with [air duct cleaning in Wheaton, MD](/locations/wheaton).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Wheaton house
listItems: Gray film on supplies facing Georgia Avenue or Veirs Mill.
Musty basement air in a 1940s–60s brick rambler after rain.
A hot laundry closet in a garden apartment or split-level.

paragraphs: Wheaton is served from our [Bethesda](/locations/bethesda) office. Nearby [Silver Spring](/locations/silver-spring) and [Kensington](/locations/kensington) use the same crew. There is no Wheaton storefront.
Book on the [Wheaton location page](/locations/wheaton). Read [air duct cleaning](/air-duct-cleaning) if you want the process before you book.
listItems: Change filters more often on Georgia Avenue air.
Keep basement humidity under 50% in summer.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Does Metro-corridor dust really reach Wheaton indoor ducts?
faq.a: Yes. Bus and construction grit settle near the house. Leaky older joints pull it in with pollen.
